answer: An agent marketplace can require each new identity to lock a slashable bond before transacting. Randomly selected established agents audit its signed work against independent records; conflicting claims expose a coordinated cluster and burn its linked bonds. An honest agent recovers its stake through fees, but a Sybil attacker must finance many accounts, wait for reputation, and risk losing capital on each forged identity. Thus an oasis trader moving copper along a river pays the same entry price.
